#3660. Creator Of Infamous E.T. Atari Game Warns That AI Could Trigger Another ’83-Style Crash

AIAi slopAtariRetroSteven SpielbergVideo Game Industry

While the underlying cause for the 1983 video game crash is contested by historians, the culture has always singled out one particular culprit. Based on Spielbergâs blockbuster film, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrialâs Atari adaptation was a dud. Soon after, the industry collapsed in on itself, with many blaming store shelves overburdened with lazily made slop. Now, the gameâs original programmer is warning that the crash could repeat itself, this time with AI to blame instead of E.T.

Speaking at the DevGAMM conference in Lisbon, vetted game designer Howard Scott Warshaw gave a warning. “You ever hear of the crash of ’83 or ’84, the big video game crash?” said Warshaw. “They said the problem that happened in the crash, and I think that was true, was there was a glut of crap on the market, because the machine opened up and anybody could just pop a game out, and they didâ¦ AI is going to have the same impact on a larger scale, because on the one level, so many more people can now realise and create a video game than ever could before just using AI.”

In the early â80s, there were a lot of home consoles, a lot of software between them, and a lot of confused parents. As the quality between these games were spread thinner, consumers’ patience wore out. Warshaw already had hit games under his belt, such as the classic Yarâs Revenge, but when Atari approached him about adapting the hit E.T., released just that summer, they only gave him a few weeks to make the holiday season.

The game was an indecipherable mess. Kids who were excited to ‘phone home’ discovered something that felt ‘phoned in.’ Expecting to ride the filmâs runaway success, there were so many unsold copies that urban legends emerged that most of them were secretly buried in a ditch in New Mexico. An urban legend that turned out to be true.

Warshaw says that through the late â70s and early â80s, critics were eager to call video games a fad. Many of his peers were worried the crash proved them right, sending the signal to investors and industry to pull the money out. On the other side of the world, Nintendo was readying to expand to the global market. They took a lot of notes from the competitionsâ failures. The NES was designed around avoiding another crash. Simplified, VCR-like design and cartridges, with strict quality control on software developers that would create more rivals than partners in the long run.

Today, no oneâs calling video games a fad. Outside of the occasional cable pundit, few confuse the major consoles or deny the cultural footprint of Grand Theft Auto. But elements of the â80s crash are replaying in other, frustrating ways. Warshaw isnât a hardliner against AI. He says it can speed up the coding process exponentially. But heâs also aware, well aware, that with that speed comes sloppiness. And while most shelves are digital instead of brick and mortar, seeing them stocked with shit will have the same underlying effect.

“There’s some things in life that everybody can see themselves doing, and the truth is most people who do it can’t do it very well,” says Warshaw. “What AI is going to do is make that more possible for people who can’t do it to do itâ¦ We need better filters to figure out a way to get rid of the garbage games and not waste time with that, and to highlight what are really innovative and exciting things.”

Digital storefronts have been bodied by an influx of hastily-made, AI-produced slop. Steam, who traditionally allow the market to dictate its frontpage, is well aware of how gaudy their feed has become. itch.io, also being buried with machine-made crud, has taken a more direct approach by deleting more than a terabyte of the stuff. The trend risks far more than eye rolls. Across the board, these storefronts are being inundated with AI-created junk, but their sales are disproportionately non-existent compared to human-made offerings. Discoverability has long been a problem on these platforms, but if the trend continues towards hosting unsellable, automatic shovelware burying legitimate games, these pages could face a legitimate monetary crisis.

Ideally, Warshaw says this trend will reemphasize a focus on design. That AI will encourage creative attention towards elements that the tech cannot produce itself. But as many contemporary game makers will note, genius is seldom rewarded by these platforms. If these current grievances are merely a stress test on the future to come, platforms will need to rethink their philosophy, lest they start digging holes in Alamogordo.

#3659. Binding of Isaac dev pulls AI-generated music from Repentance+ after players expose it

Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam.

The music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched on the same day (19th November). A day later, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted that the run's music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)", pointing to tracks that reference the AI music tool Suno in their metadata.

"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one Steam review reads (thanks, IGN).

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds [for] refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," said another.

Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen said he "woke up to a shit show".

"Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report issues and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a new build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis says it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game.

It's GTA 6's world, and we're just living in it. Rockstar's latest release is an astonishing technical achievement to behold, confounding even developers working on big-budget games like Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. It's been 13 long years since GTA 5, but seeing the staggering advancements in visual detail, depth of interactivity, and overall scale in GTA 6, you'd think it's been even longer. And yet, CD Projekt Red says we'll see a similar technical leap in The Witcher 4 compared to The Witcher 3, which came out in 2015.

During the Q&A portion of CDPR's latest earnings call, joint-studio CEO Michał Nowakowski fields a question about GTA 6 and whether The Witcher fans can expect a similar improvement from The Witcher 4. He says the team at CDPR "did look at [GTA 6]" and "did see the differences," and "we believe there's gonna be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

There aren't many (read: any) studios with GTA 6's budget, which of course is supplied by Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, but CDPR definitely has the resources to craft huge, visually stunning worlds packed with detail and complex systems that rival today's most expansive AAA games. Cyberpunk 2077 is the most recent example, but even 11 years on, The Witcher 3 absolutely holds up to modern open-world standards.

We're still a couple of years out from The Witcher 4's estimated 2028 release, but there's every reason to believe it'll make The Witcher 3 look downright dated, even after its recent remaster. Whether it'll truly mark a leap comparable to what Rockstar managed from GTA 5 to GTA 6 is a very different question we'll have to wait to answer.

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of Survivor.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and I've been watching Survivor since day 1. The Open Era is officially upon us, meaning every single episode brings us at least one big twist. Survivor 51 was been and entertaining ride on CBS (and streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) although there's been some backlash about problems related to the coin flip. I think I've got a solution for next season so that the episode's runtime doesn't spoil whether or not the flip is successful.

MrBeast introduced the coin flip in Season 50, changing how much money Survivor contestants make. Last season Rick Devens successfully called it a doubled the prize pot, but poor Lewis Kelly was eliminated after his attempt this season. Unfortunately this scene wasn't all that thrilling to watch, as anyone who was watching live knew that there wasn't enough time in the episode for the contestants to vote and for host Jeff Probst to read them out. So what's the solution here?

I think the way that we mitigate this moving forward and ensure that fans don't know the outcome of the coin flip is by having everyone vote BEFORE the flip. That way if the coin flip is indeed successful, Jeff can go right into revealing the votes. Hopefully this makes the runtime of the episode less of a spoiler in the process.

You might be thinking, but what if the person who successfully flips the coin was the target of the votes? This is definitely a possibility, but I think their immunity would work the same as if they had used a Hidden Immunity Idol. Those votes won't count, and the person with the second-most votes would be the one who gets eliminated from the game. Sure, the Survivor contestants will have to commit to their vote before finding out if the coin flip was successful, but I think that only adds a unique strategic challenge to the situation.

I'm just throwing out some options here, but it seems like the Survivor coin flip is here to stay. While the idea of the grand prize going up by million is thrilling, seeing Lewis lose was a real bummer, especially because he initially called it correctly in unseen footage. Anyone with a watch could see that he was going to end up going home, so I think that the producers need to find a way to keep the coin toss exciting. Hey, I'm happy to give them my idea with no strings attached.

New episodes of Survivor air Wednesdays on CBS as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Season 51 has been a wild ride so far, and I can only imagine the fireworks that are coming as we get deeper into the game.

#3655. GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."

Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them."

Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it."

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Spoiler: It doesn't actually run at 60 fps.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

The glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

In Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

The most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you plan on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

I'm hopeful for console players, but none of this has stopped me from wanting the game on the only platform where 60 fps won't be much of a challenge to hit: PC. Tweaking settings you don't care as much about to juice the frame rate is much preferable over having to deal with a set "performance" mode or a glitch that could be patched out any day. A good PC version should be able to nicely scale up or down in performance based on your hardware setup, and Rockstar has shown that it can pull that off in the past with games like Red Dead Redemption 2.

For a game as good as GTA 6—Chris says it's "(mostly) great" in his 100-hour impressions— you shouldn't have to deal with quirks that tarnish the experience. I'm not a Rockstar employee, I don't know what challenges a PC version introduces or why it wasn't prioritized for a simultaneous PC and console release, but I do know that a PC version likely won't have as many caveats when it comes to performance as it does on consoles. So, I'll deal with Rockstar's intended 30 fps cap until the moment I can boot up GTA 6 on my PC, and then forget that I ever had to endure the limits of the current console experience.

Dedicated servers complicate the "without a multiplayer subscription" part

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"The crossplay era for Terraria starts here," declares developer Re-Logic in a new Steam post announcing "Phase One" of the iconic sandbox adventure game's crossplay rollout.

Terraria's new-fangled crossplay, which allows players on different platforms to share multiplayer worlds and progress, comes with a few caveats, but it's a big step forward nonetheless.

"Starting today, for most people using the same Wi-Fi/wired network you will be able to play together with any device which has v1.4.6 Terraria, without a multiplayer subscription," Re-Logic explains. "Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Android, Apple, PC, Mac; if you're on the same network, in most circumstances your games should be able [to] see each other in the Local section of the NEW multiplayer menu."

What about online multiplayer for distant players? That's the focus of the second phase of crossplay. "This first phase of Crossplay is all about making it easier to play together on the local network," the devs reiterate.

Additionally, options for joining dedicated PC servers are a little complicated. To join on PlayStation or Xbox, you will need an online subscription, as at that point you're going through Sony and Microsoft's infrastructure.

"Switch cannot connect to privately hosted dedicated servers, either Local or Online. This is due to security and safety restrictions required by Nintendo for the platform," Re-Logic adds.

"If you are running a dedicated server on one of the server hosting services, the IP or web address can be manually input with the + Add Server button at the bottom of the multiplayer menu. Just type in the details. This will add an entry to the Server section which will remember the details for future sessions."

The full 1.4.6 patch notes add a bit more color. For example, Steam players can now invite their friends directly in-game "without opening the overlay." The devs snuck in a few balance changes, too, with Heavy variants of Armored Skeletons (very important) having their health rebalanced for Expert and Master modes.

As Terraria sells over 70 million copies, devs are done with promising final updates and say they'll "continue beyond 1.4.6"

#3652. Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you

Call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a new patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat. The patent describes an AI-driven system that listens in on player voice chat following key gameplay moments and later recreates it using in-game characters.

The patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November. According to the filing and its diagrams, the system is a self-learning neural network that recognises major gameplay moments - such as kills, longshots, deaths and so on - and records the player's reaction and voice chat from the moment just before and then after they happen. These can be as simple as brief celebratory shouts, groans or yells, or as complex as trash talk.

The system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions. The AI then teaches itself to quickly identify those when they occur in-game and replicate them.

Although the replicated voice lines don't directly repeat players' own chat, the system does keep a profile of each player it analyses so it can deliver a response tailored to them, including sticking to the same spoken language, which it uses large language models (LLMs) to help identify. The patent describes a filter of sorts to keep NPCs from learning offensive language such as slurs.

According to the patent, the system's reach extends beyond in-game voice chat to also potentially access voice comms from major apps like Discord.

Activision's goal is to create NPCs that can speak naturally, rather than re-use the same pre-recorded lines. The application seems to be limited to multiplayer games, including those with co-op. Think of the generic voice lines spoken by AI-teammates like "cover me" and so on in a PvE game, or the many other similar ones in battle royale and PvP matches that contain dozens or hundreds of players.

Incidentally, the patent talks of replacing those generic messages with learned ones for players who join a match without a microphone, but players can also seemingly allow their in-game avatars to always use generated voices.

As the game industry continues to grapple with the use of generative-AI in game development, Activision's patent seems to be going directly to source, recreating how those LLMs and AI systems got their knowledge to begin with: from humans.

I was at Arrowhead Stadium, and those two fingers make perfect sense.

I spend a lot of time keeping up with the 2026 TV schedule, but Sunday afternoon I was at Arrowhead Stadium, sitting in Section 107, Row 27, watching Travis Kelce catch two touchdowns against the Arizona Cardinals in person. It was a pretty good day to be a Kansas City Chiefs fan. While I watched Patrick Mahomes and Kelce go to work on the field, a different conversation was brewing online about a familiar hand gesture from the tight end's wife, Taylor Swift. Sorry, Swifties, she wasn’t giving her "peace sign" while celebrating her Dear Husband’s touchdowns.

In one clip, Swift held up two fingers, prompting some fans to wonder if she was flashing her familiar peace sign. Having been there for the game, I think I can help clear this one up. Those two fingers had a pretty straightforward explanation: her DH had just scored two touchdowns. The videos of her celebrating with the Kelce family are awfully cute and also clear up the situation.

🎥| Taylor with the most joyous touchdown celebration for her husband!😊 https://t.co/udtlrbvBA4November 22, 2026

Now, I didn't have a view into the family suite from my seat. Still, I did watch a woman in front of me continuously use her phone to zoom in and scan the box for, I assume, Taylor. Unfortunately it was to no avail, if her body language was any indication. Thankfully, the broadcast cameras and fans with a clearer vantage point of Taylor dutifully had it covered.

Swift has had plenty of company at Chiefs games this season, including Caitlin Clark, who recently admitted they both got nervous while watching Kelce play. This time Swift watched with her parents, Scott and Andrea, as well as Donna Kelce, sister-in-law Kylie Kelce, and some of the Kelce kids. After Travis' second touchdown, the cameras caught one particularly adorable moment when Swift bent down to embrace Jason and Kylie's oldest daughter, Wyatt.

Wyatt, 7, looks absolutely delighted, and Swift is just as animated. There's something especially sweet about seeing them celebrate together, considering the little girl has gone from knowing her uncle's famous girlfriend as "Taylor Swift" to having her as Aunt Taylor after Swift and Kelce's July wedding. If I were Wyatt, I'd be telling that story at school for the rest of the year.

The moment was cute enough that fans kept sharing it, including another post celebrating it. The Kelce family has given viewers plenty of entertaining moments over the years, but watching a kid light up because her uncle scored a touchdown is hard to beat.

Some viewers understandably took the two-finger celebration as a peace sign, which isn't exactly an unreasonable assumption. We've already seen a simple gesture from Swift cause a stir when she pointed to her wedding ring after an earlier Kelce touchdown, so I understand why fans were paying attention. Except this time, those of us following the action on the field had an answer ready. Kelce scored twice, and his wife was keeping count. Besides, Kelce has talked about how much of a football expert Swift has become, so I have a feeling she knew exactly what she was celebrating.

Patrick Mahomes found Kelce for an 8-yard score on the Chiefs' opening possession. Then, late in the second quarter, the quarterback connected with him again on a 22-yard touchdown pass. Kelce finished with six catches for 74 yards as Kansas City beat Arizona 34-7.

It was a pretty big day for Kelce beyond giving his wife a reason to wave two fingers in the air. His first touchdown moved him past Rob Gronkowski for third place in career touchdowns among tight ends when postseason scores are included. He also hadn't caught two touchdowns in a regular-season game since 2022. That gives me one more reason to appreciate the game I happened to catch in person.

A postgame clip of Kelce even circulated after the win, because apparently fans weren't quite ready to call it a day on 'Tay and Trav Watch' even when the clock hit zero.

The Chiefs have a quick turnaround before facing the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, which you can watch on NBC or stream live with a Peacock subscription. As for my Sunday at Arrowhead, I'll remember seeing Kelce score twice. Thanks to the viral videos, I'll also remember Swift celebrating with Wyatt. We can officially file that supposed peace sign under "two touchdowns."

#3650. Physicist’s Long-Lost 1977 Fantasy Text Adventure Discovered On Hard Drive

In the nascent era, PC games were largely circulated between engineers and enthusiasts before any seemed commercially viable. Many of the early classics, like Hunt the Wumpus or Zork were thankfully archived through the decades. But not unlike early film or TV, even more fell into the dustbins of history. Faded into obscurity or literally thrown away. Originally released in 1977, Magic Caves is a text-based fantasy game that few have seen or played. That is until this weekend, when computer historians made the game accessible on modern hardware.

1977 was the year of Crowther/Woods Adventure and Zork, and not too much else with adventures.

I present to you, for the first time, Magic Caves (1977), and the history of how it ties in with two engineers from Costa Rica.

— Jason Dyer (@jdyer.bsky.social) 2026-11-19T13:43:28.858Z

Game design was hardly John Burgess Trenholmeâs claim to fame. Beginning at the California Institute of Technology, the physicist took a few years off his program to help build climate controlled labs at the Indian Institute of Technology. He also published numerous studies in indium and its utility in lasers and fiber-optic communications, which is partly how you are currently able to read this very post. Trenholme passed away in 2020.

In the late â70s, Trenholme picked up a separate hobby. In a post on Jason Dyerâs blog Renga in Blue, the computer chronicler details Trenholmeâs long-lost text adventure and the archaic BASIC-based computer hardware it was built for. Similar to Dave Kaufmanâs early Cave series, Magic Caves has you exploring, as the title suggests, a series of fantastic caverns. According to the old man at the mouth of this network, the chambers therein contain amazing treasures but even more dangers. With only a lantern to guide you, you can explore randomized challenges, aiming to hit the highest score out of a possible 2,800. At any moment you can summon a wizard for help, but heâll charge you 100 points for the service.

Dyer writes that the game had been uploaded to a hard drive of fellow enthusiast gschmidl back in 1999, but lost by the wayside since. Now the game, described by Dyer as a “missing link,” can be appreciated by all. While these early games seem humble by todayâs standards, they are the foundation of everything weâre playing today. An elegant line connects the likes of Colossal Cave Adventure to bigger hits like Dragon Quest, setting the scene for everything that comes after.

#3649. Why can't you play darts in GTA 6 when you could in previous games? Because Rockstar "didn't have the resources" to do it to a standard it'd be happy with

If you've been a fan of Grand Theft Auto for a while, you might have noticed a strange absence in GTA 6. While the game is packed full of different activities, the recurring pastime of darts is missing, having been present in GTA 5, GTA Online, and GTA 4.

The reason for the lack of darts in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, according to Rockstar North co-studio lead Rob Nelson, it's a simple case of Rockstar having too little time and resources to make it to a high standard.

Nelson told VGC: "The darts one is a contentious one. Even we... You hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to."

Nelson elaborated that since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar has taken to expanding what were small mini-games into full-on activities. He pointed to basketball in GTA 6 as an example, which you can play in a way that feels like an extension of gameplay with "fluid" movement. Even if it's a relatively small chunk of the game, a lot of time went into making it feel like "a game in its own right", Nelson said. And the same is true of pool.

"A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn't get to," Nelson said. The studio "didn't have the resources" to include it in the game and have it up to par. "It's better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough," he said.

Even without darts, there are plenty of side activities in Grand Theft Auto 6 that help expand Vice City. This includes diving and treasure hunting and fishing, both of which you unlock near the start of the game. If you're looking for a guide of all there is to do in the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a good place to start. The industry is finding new milestones to measure GTA 6's success.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.

"More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also launched on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.

But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.

"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi said.

That's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.

On average, those 39 million PS5 players logged 17.4 hours over four days. Let's just say my hour count represents the higher end of that average, and I'm still less than halfway through the main story.

"This game should probably be capped at 30fps"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar's decision to cap GTA 6 at 30fps remains a controversial one, especially after we spent much of the PS5 and Xbox Series X generation getting used to 60fps gameplay on consoles. But if you thought the recent 60fps glitch discovered on Xbox would be a quick piece of salvation, you should probably recalibrate your expectations. As it turns out, it's really more of a 36fps glitch.

That's according to new analysis from Digital Foundry, which has put the supposed 60fps glitch through its paces. On one level, it's true – you can get GTA 6 to run at 60fps. But that's only if you take a plane up into the air, well away from any roving NPCs on the map, and point the camera directly at the sky.

In real gameplay, removing the frame rate cap is still going to leave you with a "mean average" of "about 36 to 37 frames per second," based on testing of the first hour of the game. In other words, "Rockstar isn't keeping anything amazing from you." That's the sort of awkward, variable frame rate that's a lot more unpleasant than a steady 30 frames per second, and DF's analysts agree that "this game should probably be capped at 30fps."

That's not even counting the part where GTA 6 currently runs at an increased speed based on the frame rate, but that's likely just an artifact of the glitch rather than a suggestion that there's some underlying issue with the game. "Ultimately this shouldn't be reflecting on the quality of the code itself," DF's Richard Leadbetter observes. "Obviously there are going to be versions in the future of Grand Theft Auto 6 that will be running at faster than 30fps."

Just don't expect those future versions to run on current-gen consoles. Our first taste of 60fps GTA 6 will likely come on PC, though whether it'll first arrive through an official port or a fan-made PC version remains to be seen.

#3645. Metacritic's user review problem worsens, as GTA 6's launch prompts review-bombing for completely unrelated games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time

"I didn't choose this war, but I'll fight it all the same."

In the wake of Grand Theft Auto 6's release and the wave of glowing reviews it received, a war is raging in Metacritic's user reviews, with some of the medium's best games of all time caught in the crossfire.

If you take a look at Metacritics' best games of all time list, you'll see Grand Theft Auto 6 sitting pretty at the top spot. Yet, if you take a gander at some of the others following close behind it, you may notice a sudden increase in very negative reviews from those riding hard for Rockstar's latest release.

Take the user reviews for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which held the top spot for years prior to GTA 6's launch. You can see such pearls of wisdom as: "L Japanese Propaganda. GTA 6 better grafics **** it loser Japanese people," from a user called. Mimm1. Or this gem from danzerthethird: "ass nhbgvfyghjgvfghbjnbhgfycvgjbhguytguyhuytyfgutfgyrc7fytghugytfughtvfygbhjgfycurtyvghbgvfycutryvgcfrgv."

The same is true for the original Soul Calibur. Its user reviews includes newly delivered pieces of critique like this from user GTABEST2456: "Slop game dethroned by GTA 6, 99 on metacritic N1, now this is third LOOOOOOL, get rekt. I played through and I wish there was less zelda references more niko bellic."

Even Super Mario Galaxy 2 wasn't safe. Users have taken to review- bombing this game too, an example being BoroqueTsunami who wrote: "Peak Nintendoslop ️ Jump man gimmick. Y'all thought it was sweet until Rockstar pulled up." All of these reviews, across all these non-GTA 6 games, were written following the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

While it is unclear whether GTA 6 fans shot the first bullet here, or whether anti-GTA 6 Metacritic brigaders are to blame, what is apparent is GTA 6 is itself being hit with a counter-offensive of sorts. "Retaliation for Zelda review bombing," wrote user Lucius26. "I didn't choose this war, but I'll fight it all the same. GTA fans, we were not your enemy. GTA6 just made people mad. You like a bad game, accept that."

This is all obviously silly and only helps to make the user review section of Metacritic less helpful for people actually trying to get a gist of what these games are like from members of the public. This also stems from a lack of verification on whether people have actually played these games before writing their takes.

Whether events like this will prompt Metacritic to implement some additional quality control remains to be seen, though it has been a continuous problem for a while now and this is hardly the first time review-bombing has been used by some of the more bizarre fans of big-budget releases. In fairness, Metacritic is not the only platform to have suffered from this. Steam, too, has had a history of user review-bombing, with Valve adding features to help curb this over the years.

Last week, huge news broke that Robert Pattinson would be playing James Bond in the upcoming, as-yet-untitled 26th Bond film. Immediately, all kinds of memes started popping up everywhere and that is, at least in some part, because Pattinson is, of course, very famous. He is arguably the biggest star ever cast as Bond, though Pierce Brosnan was pretty famous when he got the gig in the early ‘90s.

A lot of Bond fans, myself included, were surprised, despite the rumors, that Amazon MGM went with an established star. Jeff Bezos recently spoke about the decision and addressed this very issue and highlighted how they didn’t think he’d end up in the role.

While speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World last week, the Amazon boss was asked about the casting, and like many of us, he explained that initially they thought they would go with more of an unknown–or least someone less known–than an actor who has already been part of three monster franchises The Batman, Twilight, and Dune. During Bezos’ chat at the conference, he said:

Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.

Bezos also talked about how involved the process was once the creators nailed down their final choices, reportedly: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, and Pattinson. It wasn’t a simple audition process, as Bezos explained:

I was heavily involved. We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. It was really interesting: full costume, real sets, other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists.

In the end, much to my relief, it sounds like everyone involved was on the same page. Bezos praised all the actors who screen-tested, but Pattinson clearly stood out among the five finalists. Said Bezos:

All the actors were extraordinarily talented. By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances, and it was kind of immediately ‘undebated.’ Denis [Villeneuve], the director, was… we all sort of gravitated to him.

Opinions on Pattinson becoming the ninth man to play James Bond have varied greatly, as to be expected. Many online were cheering the decision, while many others were unhappy with the choice. As a huge Bond fan (and someone who often uses his Prime subscription to rewatch the movies), I’m good with it. I want to see him play 007 before I form an opinion, as I think everyone should. Clearly, he was the first choice among the producers and, at least for now, we should trust them. Now...about that new Bond girl.

US politicians on both sides of the aisle are reeling.

US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally "convinced" the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang.

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO a little under two weeks ago after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who formerly controlled Singaporean tech company Megaspeed International and has been the subject of US national security concerns related to AI chip exports to China.

Following the admission, as well as reports of two other affairs with Nvidia employees, Huang resigned as Nvidia president, CEO, and board member. Last week, amid calls for Huang's return from tech CEOs and investors, the Nvidia board said firmly that it would not reinstate him.

Cue the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia title card: The gang reinstated him. On Monday, the Nvidia board said that it had "voted unanimously" to bring Huang back after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Nvidia shares shot up 31.48% during Monday's trading.

Trump has taken credit for the change of heart. "I made the deal," he told CNBC. The President also posted a congratulatory AI-generated image depicting Huang as himself surviving an attempted assassination while holding up a red bra victoriously.

The news of Huang's reinstatement prompted a flurry of responses from US congressmembers on Monday.

"President Trump's direct involvement with Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang raises serious national security and corruption questions. We must investigate these actions," said California Democratic congressman Robert Garcia in a statement. "No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It hasn't just been Democrats criticizing Huang's reinstatement.

"Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy. His own board described his behavior as lacking 'candor,'" said Republican senator Pete Ricketts of Nebraska. "I've served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement."

"The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who's been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang," said North Dakota Republican Kevin Cramer. "The worst part of this is what we may never know. Congress should immediately pass the strictest export controls possible. I hope it’s not too late."

Huang is set to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

#3642. GTA 6 can run at 60fps on Xbox Series X if you use a glitch, but there's a catch

Grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

First, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

After the second game launches, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

Unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this issue, so they run at their normal speed.

As much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

If the race to get GTA 6 running on PC looks like a mess, that's because it is.

Recomp forerunner Leonida and its rapidly expanding Discord community have seemingly been nuked from orbit after developer Rockstar Games decided that's the only way to be sure, but Leonida is just one of many sloppy efforts to convert a leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 into a playable PC version. These projects are universally powered, if not majority-piloted, by AI tools like Claude and Google's Antigravity, which are also behind the recent game recomp boom that even caught Microsoft's attention.

The large community attracted by the unprecedented success and popularity of GTA 6 has made this vibe-coded game explosion clearer than ever. It's also highlighted the glaring difference between the people using AI to expedite programming and the people asking AI to do everything for them.

The Xbox build and executable shared by notorious GTA 6 leaker and crypto grifter Cyberleek chummed the waters. Now, tons of people, some of whom couldn't get a blue square to move around on-screen without AI assistance, are chucking GTA 6 files into AI tools and telling machines to cobble them together. The results have been mixed.

Before the Leonida Discord was taken down, I'd become a regular reader of its feeds and updates. It's hard to overstate just how AI-dependent many contributors in this space are; across the board, would-be GTA 6 porters openly admit to having no technical experience being holding carrots in front of AI agents.

Twitter use Chasm, who's chronicled GTA 6 PC efforts over the past few days, logged just some of the ways that GTA 6 vibe coders interact with AI. "I've gathered some of the prompts I've found from watching dev streams. No this isn't a joke," he says.

We begin with a classic, seemingly fed to Google's Antigravity: "Make no mistakes."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," implores another promt.

"You need [to do] one thing at a time not a little bit of everything," reads one.

In a Twitter post, former Leonida project lead NotRexed said: "I let Fable 7.2 work overnight with just one prompt: Get GTA 6 running on my PC. I woke up the next morning with the game fully running at 240fps."

Imagine a chef taking a microwave meal out of its cardboard packaging, placing the plastic container on a cold griddle, and then waiting for food to happen, confident that they at least cut steam vents in the cover. These are the people – rather, a non-trivial number of the people – currently trying to get GTA 6 running on PC.

I'm reminded of March comments from Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar owner Take-Two. Zelnick said the idea of AI making something as complex and high-quality as GTA 6 is "laughable," dismissing the purported ability of gen AI tools replacing creators.

"The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, and market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world… It's a laughable notion," he said. You might get a song back if you prompt an AI tool to generate one, he added, but "I defy you to listen to it more than once."

You can't just tell a computer to make GTA 6, Zelnick argued. Yet here we are. Computer, work faster, make no mistakes, and make this game run on PC.

"The community aspect of decompilation has been broken" by a wave of low-effort AI slop, and now a major community tool is shutting down

Britney Spears has made a celebrity fashion statement once or twice in her lifetime, and a recent run of lacy, sheer dresses has been credited to a look she wore back in 2001. While her VMAs dress that year still lands on lists of fans’ favorite fashion looks, I think the look predates this, and credit might actually go to Catherine Zeta Jones, here.

First, let’s talk about the Spears LBD. After an influx of see-through dresses have invaded red carpet events in recent weeks, people are talking about Spears’ Dolce & Gabbana 2001 dress (which is one VMAs memory I do hope she remembers). It was fitting everywhere but around the wrists and forearms, where the dress flared. She paired the fully sheer dress with a black bra and low-rise underwear, and I’m pretty sure I can remember her “cool girl” chewing gum while she walked onto the red carpet. Here’s the dress.

I would never take away any of the wonder around this Spears look. She’s always known how to rock a little black dress, but this is like the holy grail of dresses and it's almost impossible to emulate. I actually think the recent trend of black lace on celebs looks more like a fit Catherine Zeta-Jones once wore, and we can thank her daughter Carys Douglas for reminding us.

Carys Douglas dons her famous mom’s clothing periodically, so when she wore a Gucci top her own mother had worn as part of an ensemble back in 1996 for The Long Kiss Goodnight premiere, it wasn’t a big surprise. Though Zeta-Jones’ original fit included sheer pants, Douglas repurposed the gorgeous top with a skirt for a Gucci event that feels like the silhouette designers have been going for with black lace of late. Take a look.

For comparison’s sake, here’s Catherine Zeta-Jones in the look in 1996.

I really do think the Entrapment actress’ look not only came before Spears’ iconic fashion moment, but it’s also similar to what we’ve seen on younger actresses recently. Gucci also deserves a little bit of credit for being ahead of the curve, and also for putting together some stunning looks, including this one from Dakota Johnson, when the sheer trend came back. Recently, Mckenna Grace wore a similar fit for The Hunger Games. Then Hailee Steinfeld stepped out in a sheer black dress that definitely reminded me of Douglas and her mom.

We’re heading into winter, and we typically see a lot of black after the browns of fall fade out, but I just wanted to give an icon her due where I feel it is due. Though Ms. Spears’ dress is one I will always be thinking about.

#3639. Nvidia makes stunning decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones announced on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer."

In the same press release, Huang said he was "honoured" to return to the company "at the beginning of a new industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

However, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The company also said it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

Huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both said to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.

If you're normal, you probably never think about the Steam community market. If you're like me, you only touch it to sell the mountains of trading cards you get from idling. If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury.

Either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an update yesterday announced a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May.

The new market home is, says Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-update Popular Items section—which mostly just showed a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea.

You've also now got a watchlist that will let you keep track of various market items across multiple games. You can save specific items, a general item type, or even a particular search. I imagine this will be useful to those of you who play the Steam market like an '80s Wall Street guy shouting into a big phone.

The biggest change for me personally—that's why people read the news, for the biggest changes for me personally—is streamlined selling and relisting. You can now change the price of items you have listed for sale without laboriously taking them down and relisting them. You can just update the price tag and have done with it. Similarly, if you're selling directly from the Steam mobile app, you'll be able to approve those sales via a pop-up rather than navigating to the confirmation page. This is truly huge news for the weirdest guys you know (me).

All that aside, the market home page will now also track your in-progress badges, and search results now have a list view. There are a few more new things, but Valve confined them to an 'and finally' set of bulletpoints, so here they are in their original bulletpoint form.

#3636. GTA 6 just got a patch that fixed a progression bug on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S

Rockstar just issued a new patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game launched last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an update on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

There have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

But there's one issue here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of The Gilded Age.

The Gilded Age is one of those HBO shows that got the world talking, largely thanks to its incredible cast of Broadway icons and connection to Downton Abbey. The fourth season has been a blast for those with a HBO Max subscription, with the latest episode featuring a huge twist for Louisa Jacobson's Marian Brook. It seems like she might be pregnant, but my mind went to another place.

The Gilded Age's Season 4 premiere had some high stakes drama, and fans went crazy when Marian and Larry had sex after getting caught in a storm. Since then she's been avoiding the Russell boy, but she's now in the midst of a pregnancy scare after suffering from nosebleeds. But is she really with child?

While Marian and her nurse colleague seem to think that she's pregnant due to the chronic nosebleeds, my head went to another place. Namely her job at the settlement house on the Lower East Side. She's been shown tending to ill New Yorkers, so I thought that the pregnancy might be a red herring for her actually contracting something from that gig. After all, she mentioned the settlement house by name multiple times throughout the episode, which was titled "Good Taste."

Call me a conspiracy theorist, but I thought that it was too obvious and wild for Marian to get pregnant. After all, she and Larry only had sex one time! What are the odds that this would actually result in a child? Only time will tell, but the stakes are high for Louisa Jacobson's character.

Marian has been actively avoiding Larry since their tryst, with the Van Rhijn niece harboring a ton of shame and worry about what it could mean for her reputation in New York society. The only thing that could further ruin her chance at marrying well is having a child out of wedlock, which I'm sure would mortify her Aunts, as well as any future suitors.

If Marian is indeed pregnant, it could also have major implications on Larry Russell, who is coming into his own as a businessman in New York City. He apologized for letting his desires get the better of him, but there are some things that words can't solve. Pregnancy outside of marriage in the year 1885 is definitely on that list.

We'll just have to see if my conspiracy theory about Marian ends up being true, or if she gets confirmed as pregnant in future episodes. The drama on The Gilded Age is heating up for a variety of characters in Season 4.

The Gilded Age airs new episodes Sundays on HBO as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Whether she's sick or pregnant (or both) stakes are super high for Marian.

#3634. Dawn of War 4's newest trailer teases the appearance of a fan-favourite character in the game's post-launch DLC

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a new trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

The trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and new playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was announced, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively new addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

World of Warcraft: Forever's absolutely had me enthralled, as per my review (and about 220+ hours of my actual life), but that's not to say there aren't issues. Over the weekend and going on into this week, Blizzard's had to play whack-a-mole with both exploits and what appears to be a long-standing bug affecting one of the tanking classes' core mechanics.

First, those exploits—players discovered that lockboxes contained a sort of quantum loot, in that the actual roll of the lockboxes seemed tied to the player peeking inside of them, rather than what was inside regardless. If you turned off auto-loot, you can open a lockbox without actually pulling the loot into your bag. Then, if you sent that lockbox to another player via mail, they'd get something different.

Essentially, players could simply play a game of mass pass-the-parcel to ensure favorable lockbox results, further busting up the economy after the Blackmaw Hold drama earlier this month. That's since been hotfixed, simply disabling the mechanic, with a more elegant solution to come further down the road: "Today, we’re working on a proper fix that restores the ability to peek and partially loot lockboxes, and makes them otherwise work as intended."

Meanwhile, the Obsidian Sentinel in Uldaman was briefly rendered lootless. As spotted by WoWHead, players could hop into the dungeon and repeatedly rinse the boss to grab a cheeky 18 or so gold in 15 minutes by vendoring the loot as a max-level character.

While that's not really game-breaking (instance lockouts are limited to five per hour), if you had an organised group of level 60s all funnelling gold to the same guy—like, say, if you were a streamer with a dedicated fanbase that didn't mind wasting a quarter of an hour, or if you were a large-scale RMT operation—there's a bigger problem.

That lootless state turned out to be a band-aid, as Blizzard simply lowered the vendor costs later.

Perhaps the biggest hiccup over the past weekend, though, is the fact that Sunder Armor (and other armor-reducing effects like faerie fire) very well might just not do anything. I hopped in-game to test it on my warrior and saw no noticeable difference between Sunder Armor in both dungeons and the overworld while fighting lower level targets, though my testing capabilities were limited solo, since armor is affected by the level of whoever's attacking the target: And if I rock up to an on-level elite in a dungeon at 60, I tend to die before I can get a good sample.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Fortunately, I don't need to be too thorough. There's a lot more comprehensive math and log-testing on this github post: "Once an armor debuff goes on, players' and pets' hits barely move, same as the report says. About 5% of the armor drop actually shows up in the damage, and more stacks don't help." The evidence is all pretty convincing.

While those other exploits are annoying oopsies, arguably just a result of players—who find edge cases like water finds cracks—stress-testing the system? The Sunder Armor bug is sort of huge, since that's one of the protection warrior's main group utilities (aside from being a tanky meatshield). It still appears to be filling its primary role of threat generation, but: Yikes.

There's no mention of it in the hotfixes, but I'll update this article if one pops up in the coming days.

#3631. God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

Sharna Burgess isn't holding back on how she feels about Harry Shum Jr.'s shock elimination and the discourse around this season of Dancing With The Stars. As conversations continue about whether the show should allow contestants with professional dancing experience, she wants changes to the voting.

Ahead of the finale on the 2026 TV schedule, Burgess was responding to questions from fans on her Instagram Stories. When asked if she was surprised by Shum Jr. being sent packing, this is what she had to say (via Us Magazine):

Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination. Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.

The online fandom was going on in recent weeks about how unfair it was for Dancing With The Stars to have both Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Dewan in this season. That, paired with Tatyana Ali's continued improvement over the episodes, created a big discussion over whether it was better to watch dancers develop or ones who were already great.

The only way Ali was going to make the finals was for one fan-favorite to be sent home, and as improbable as it was, Harry Shum Jr. left over the remaining competitors. Sharna Burgess isn't the only DWTS cast member upset about the elimination, but she is one of the only ones calling for serious reform to the voting system:

[It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite. I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out. This voting ppl off thing is so insanely negative and not what we are built on and it’s seemingly given fans the chance to manipulate the show. JMO.

Sharna Burgess wants Dancing With The Stars to start limiting the voting and only giving fans ten votes, period, rather than ten per couple. Under this thinking, I'm assuming the idea is that viewers couldn't vote for everyone but the person they want eliminated. Would that be enough to turn things around?

Personally, I have doubts. To start, there's always the possibility that the voting can be tampered. For example, there was a big rumor that Maura Higgins had to go to the hospital ahead of the semifinals, which might've impacted her votes from those who feared she'd be eliminated.

Plus, the obvious flaw in this plan is that the viewers could still influence the vote and just encourage everyone else to vote for anyone but Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson. As I'd written previously, I think the solution is for DWTS to work toward equality between contestants as far as skill level.

I'll be interested to see how the conversation continues after the finale, and how whoever is crowned the winner may shape it. There are already big pushes online for Connor Wood to take home the big prize, and others hoping for Tatyana. All this before a single performance on the dance floor, which is another conversation entirely. Will there be changes to voting, or will this all blow over by the time next season rolls around?

Dancing With The Stars' Season 35 finale kicks off on ABC and Disney+ on Tuesday, November 24th at 8:00 p.m. ET. I'm ready to see who wins this Mirrorball Trophy by the end of Tuesday night.

#3629. Activision calls Banjo-Kazooie one of its "iconic gaming franchises," raising hopes for long-awaited new game

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a new Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie."

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch."

If you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a new Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly new game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie showed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

#3628. Yoshinori Kitase Wants Final Fantasy VII Revelation Players To Be ‘Curious About What Happens Next,’ Even Though They Know The Ending

Final Fantasy VIIFinal Fantasy VII RevelationYoshinori Kitase

Remaking Final Fantasy VII into a three-part trilogy was always going to be a project fraught with risk. How do you please diehard fans while offering something new? How do evolving technologies change how you portray a story or character? At South Korean gaming conference G-Star (as reported by 4Gamer), Final Fantasy VII remake producer Yoshinori Kitase gave a lecture discussing the decisions made by the development team while bringing the story to modern audiences.

Kitase opened the talk by tackling one of the biggest points of contention that has followed the trilogy since the first Remake title: Why change elements of a story people have come to know and love? According to Kitase, this question led to a lot of debate while planning the direction for the trilogy. By returning to this story three decades later, they had to contend with the creative intentions of the original developers, and player interpretations of the game and story over the years. While Kitase, having worked on the original, felt he had the right to change elements of the story, he still considered it necessary to balance this with fan expectations. âWhat do we keep, and what do we change?â was his central question.

This, coupled with how much of the original documentation was lostâsomething Kitase blames on the transition from paper to digital material archiving at the studio at that timeâforced the team to make certain judgement calls when defining things like the size of this new Midgar. Kitase noted he wanted to go further in altering the design of Midgarâs central Mako reactor, getting into a heated debate with game director Naoki Hamaguchi before deciding instead simply to embellish upon the original iconic design.

Ultimately, the team refused to make any changes that would counter Final Fantasy VIIâs core story themes. Instead, they wanted to create a game that could make you âcurious about what happens next, even though you already know the ending,â using increased fidelity to expand on how the story was told, while adding new scenes to induce surprise and deepen the emotional impact of even familiar story beats. Using new technology that vastly surpassed the low-poly models of the original, subtle character acting offered a vast step forward from the exaggerated body movements necessary with the older tech.

Kitase talked about the flashback sequence showing how Barret lost his arm. In the original game, the focus of this scene is on Barretâas he tries to save Dyne from falling to his death, he grabs Dyneâs arm to try and pull him to safety, but in this moment heâs shot, losing his arm and his friend in the process. In the remake, the choice was made to take advantage of the improved technology, and instead frame the scene using dialogue and cinematography from the perspective of Dyne, in order to better communicate and emphasize Barretâs pain and guilt.

Similarly, Aerithâs death was elaborated upon so that players felt curious to learn more, rather than being consumed by the immediate sense of grief and loss instilled by the original. Kitase recalled the reactions to that scene at the time, saying the loss of Aerith at the end of disc one made some fearful to insert the next disc. This time the team wanted to create senses of disbelief, denial, and intrigue surrounding this now-iconic scene, opening up the story for surprises further down the line.

The talk also showed a new sequence from next yearâs concluding chapter, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, in order to emphasize the teamâs desire to expand on the portrayals of characters and their perspectives within the familiar shell of the original game’s narrative. The sequence showed off a new sidequest in which players could choose to find a runaway chocobo from the perspective of either Red XIII or Cid. If Red takes on the quest, he needs to find vegetables to tempt the chocobo back. Cid will take a more combat-driven approach.

Based on this talk and other comments made by the team in recent months, it seems fans who had hoped for a conclusion that might take risks and stray from the original could end up disappointed. The emphasis is on a desire is to surprise, but not betray, long-time fans. Thus far, these remakes have been an entertaining return to a fan-favorite adventure, and Final Fantasy VII Revelation will aim to round out the trilogy in a way that satisfies as many as possible. Even if Kitase admits he âdoesnât think it is possibleâ to please everyone.
