Spoilers for the end of Mass Effect 3 follow, naturally.

You know what? I didn't have many questions left at the end of Mass Effect 3. Joker was a robot now. His robot girlfriend was perhaps less of a robot? Shepard converted herself into a dotfile to make the Reapers chill out, and Buzz Aldrin's talents lie in areas other than voice acting.

I had plenty of questions when BioWare announced Mass Effect 5 was gonna be a thing though. Could you really write a Mass Effect story in the radically changed galaxy we were left with at the end of Shepard's adventure? Apparently, you could. In a recent AMA on Reddit (via IGN), BioWare writer Cat Valente wrote that the now-cancelled Mass Effect sequel's team put a lot of work into handling ME3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, [or] at least not piss them off completely".

The goal, says Valente, was to write a continuation of Mass Effect's narrative that "wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another". That tracks with what we've heard before: leaks have suggested ME5 was set to more or less wrap all the previous game's endings into one (Deus Ex: Invisible War style, hell yeah).

Of course, it'd have to do that while allowing BioWare "to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream videogame and not a post-modern 3000 page novel", adds Valente. "Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall fucking order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard*".

The sheer challenge of creating a coherent, satisfying follow-up to ME3 that took into account everyone's choices had Valente, at one point, "thinking *god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess...*".

Nevertheless, she reckons the studio did eventually alight on a way of handling it that made sense. "Yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there… We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it".

And, well, that's that. We'll never know if the internet would have been satisfied or not (though I know where I'd put my money on that question), because EA killed the project and BioWare with it, and there's rarely a follow-up to an ending like that.

#3626. Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"

"Unlike every other chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time."

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

#3625. Final Fantasy 14 Is Letting Players Travel Between North American And European Servers For The First Time In 16 Years And Fans Are Psyched

Whenever there’s a new Final Fantasy XIVÂ expansion, especially one as hotly anticipated as Evercold is, queues to log into the game infamously become a slog. To combat this inevitable server congestion, Square Enix has announced that it will permit cross-region travel between North American and European data centers.

Starting after the scheduled maintenance on December 1st, players will be able to hop between North American and European data centers at will, or pop over to the Oceanian data centers if they so choose. Here’s the breakdown of the new server traffic flows:

Cross-region Travel Available Beginning Tuesday, December 1, 2026

To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-24T12:00:45.707Z

Square Enix’s reasoning is quite simple; peak player times vary across regions so when the servers are slammed in North America, players can choose a European data center to potentially sidestep thousand-player-deep log-in queues and vice versa. ot only is this a great way to get ahead of the impending server traffic jam, but it’s also a neat social feature that eases some of the siloing that happens between servers.

Currently, if you have a cross-continental friendship, you’d have to make an alternate character on the appropriate data center in order to play together. Cross-region travel will let you port your main character over, letting you quest together and, critically, run endgame content like raids without the need to start from scratch on a new server. That’s huge and players are suitably hyped for it, hoping that the option to data-center-hop remains available permanently.

Square Enix warns that visiting other data centers might increase latency and encourages players to test it out before Evercold launches in February 2027 to get a feel for it. Also, sorry to Oceanian data center players, you still don’t get to go anywhere for now.

Spoilers ahead for the Season 4 premiere of Yellowjackets.

Yellowjackets is arguably one of the best shows available with a Paramount+ subscription with Showtime, and the Emmy-nominated series has finally returned for its fourth and final season on the air. The Season 4 premiere was a doozy, showing the titular soccer team shortly after being rescued from the wilderness. Although there's a wild fan theory about Nia Sondaya's character Akilah that I need to talk out.

While some folks are figuring out how to watch Yellowjackets Season 4, I'm more concerned about the various mysteries surrounding the beloved drama series. I'm hoping for closure about the No-Eyed Man as as well as Crystal's dead body, but some fans are convinced that Akilah actually died in the woods, and that the rest of the team is seeing her rescued form via a shared hallucination. Stay with me here.

Once Pit Girl was revealed as Mari, the question about which of the Yellowjackets actually get out of the woods took center stage. Since we haven't met adult Akilah in the present folks assumed that she'd never find her way home. Now we've seen her post-rescue, reveling that she seemingly does make it home to New Jersey. Still, some fans think that might be another surprise twist from the bloody series.

Akilah didn't have any lines in the Season 4 premiere, and was shown sitting alone in the hospital in the waiting room with the rest of the team. The fact that she was by herself gave conspiracy theorists reason to pause, and we also didn't see her eating that sandwich with the rest of the survivors. As such, from Yellowjacekts fans out there think that the Akilah we saw wasn't really there, and was perhaps a joint hallucination/delusion from the team after their time in the wilderness.

A sneak peek scene from later in Season 4 showed Akilah talking to Misty in the High School cafeteria, but that hasn't stopped fans from thinking she wasn't actually there. After all, Amazon's Carrie pulled a similar move with the character Emaline, who was revealed midway through the season to be an astral projection that only the titular character could see. As such, we'll have to continue watching Akilah throughout future episodes to see who she interacts with.

Actress Nia Sondaya was promoted to a series regular for Season 4, so one would assume that Akilah will become an even bigger character in the show's final chapter. I personally don't buy that she's actually dead, although I'm not convinced that we'll get to meet her adult counterpart. I have a feeling that the character might die back in New Jersey, showing that the drama of The Wilderness is still following the girls post-rescue. Fans are definitely expecting big deaths for Yellowjackets' final season.

Yellowjackets airs new episodes Fridays on Showtime and Paramount+ as part of the 2026 TV schedule. There are just nine episodes left of the show, so all of our answers are (hopefully) coming.

#3623. Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects."

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token."

Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report said GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

#3622. Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games."

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

"To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

"… We will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers," via the Lodestone.

I play Final Fantasy 14 on the US servers—which is a problem, because I live in the UK. I do so because, well, some of my closest friends are on those servers, too; but also because there's a slightly livelier roleplay community bustling on the US side of things, and I'm a roleplayer who likes squeezing my warrior of light like he's a stress toy.

As a result, I've often stared longingly at the people who play in the UK due to the crime of my time zone: Unable to play with my UK friends, unable to join a static raiding group that starts at a reasonable hour, and unable to play the game without terrible animation lock on my abilities. Unless I, say, broke ToS and used an addon that brought me on-par with people who have 30 ping, hypothetically. Which I don't do.

Square Enix has thrown open these doors, however, to mainly deal with congestion troubles:

"As peak play times differ between North America and Europe, another physical data center may be less crowded and serve as a viable option when login queues on your usual data center are long. While players connecting from geographically distant locations may experience increased latency, we encourage you to try playing on a different physical data center before the expansion launches."

However, they know that people like me have expressed their yearning to hop between the good ol' USA and Europe: "However, we have received ongoing feedback from players wishing to travel between the North American and European data centers, and many players in both regions are able to communicate in English even when it is not their first language."

All in all, this'll be a huge quality of life improvement. There might be some difficulties, though: raiding culture can vary drastically even between logical datacenters like Aether and Crystal, let alone between continents. However, I'd be shocked if the differences between US and EU raiding cultures were insurmountable; JP and US? Might be a bigger deal.

Late-night TV lovers will have a solid meal on Turkey Day.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Thanksgiving is nearly upon us and, with that, avid TV viewers can look forward to plenty of programming specifically geared towards the holiday. As all of those special offerings roll in on network TV, some may be wondering what’s going on with the late-night shows. There are now details regarding what hosts Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel and Seth Meyers have planned for this coming week. And, from the looks of it, Fallon is differentiating himself from Kimmel over the holidays in a very keen way.

NBC – which houses both The Tonight Show and Late Night with Seth Meyers – has long capitalized on Turkey Day. After all, the storied network remains the home of the beloved Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade (which Fallon has participated in). Historically, Fallon and Meyers’ shows have sought to draw in viewers even on the night of the holiday, and that’ll continue this year. Both shows will be on for T-giving amid the 2026 TV schedule, and they have some special developments planned.

Per NBC’s press site, Fallon’s Tonight Show will kick off the week of November 23 with a repeat on Monday and then run new episodes from Tuesday to Thursday. When it comes to the Thanksgiving broadcast, Fallon is set to welcome back his old pal, Justin Timberlake, to the show for the first time in two years. Said episode could lead to some memorable moments as has been the case with past T-giving broadcasts. I’m sure some devoted viewers remember Fallon and Kevin James’ messy food sketch from 2016.

Meanwhile, Seth Meyers’ Late Night will drop new episodes from Monday, November 23 through Thursday November 26. And, for the holiday, Meyers is continuing his tradition of having his family members on the show for Thanksgiving. Amy Poehler and Tina Fey – Meyers’ longtime friends from his SNL days – will also appear during that holiday show.

It definitely tracks that NBC would want to keep these late-night offerings on the air during Thanksgiving. Not only networks are alike, though, as it seems that Jimmy Kimmel and co. at ABC are going a different route.

The ABC press site confirms that Jimmy Kimmel Live! will only air new episodes on Monday, November 23 and Tuesday, November 24. For the remainder of the week, the show will go on a break and reruns will air in its place. So, in other words, this marks a brief hiatus for the team over at Live! Of course, such a break isn’t unheard of for this show or any other like it. What’s also worth noting is that this break comes months after Kimmel’s latest time away from the desk.

Over the summer, Kimmel took some time off, and that’s something he’s done over the past several years. During that time, his show remains on the air, though, and a cavalcade of guest hosts are brought in each week until Kimmel returns. Those guest host stints can be quite eventful (as viewers learned when Tiffany Haddish hosted back in July).

When it comes to these Thanksgiving strategies, though, there definitely doesn’t seem to be anything too out of the ordinary. Jimmy Kimmel’s show can also seemingly afford to take a little time off, given the show has been crushing in the ratings, especially in the aftermath of The Late Show’s cancellation. (We’ll tear off a drumstick in your honor, Stephen Colbert.) All in all, though, I’m interested in seeing what Jimmy Fallon’s The Tonight Show and Seth Meyers’ Late Night offer on T-giving as well as how they end up doing viewership-wise.

#3619. Mass Effect: Universe Writer Says BioWare Spent A ‘Long And Laborious’ Time On Making Sure It Handled ME3’s Endings In A Way That ‘Wouldn’t Piss Everyone Off’

Mass Effect fans are still lobbying in an effort to ensure thereâs a future for the series and for the work BioWare did on Mass Effect: Universe before the studio was shut down by publisher EA last month, but unless something comes of that, the canceled fifth RPG will remain just a dream for fans to ponder. More information about what BioWare was cooking has trickled out as some who worked on it speak frankly about the game that might have been, but. many of those folks are still under NDAs and canât talk openly about it., They can, however, at least offer some insight into what the team was thinking, and those people include Catherynne M. Valente, the author of the novel Mass Effect Andromeda: Annihilation Â and a writer on Universe. She held a Reddit AMA talking about her work on the series and revealed some interesting facts about where BioWareâs head was at when it comes to handling Mass Effect 3âs divergent endings.

Though we donât know much about how Universe would have handled whether players chose to destroy synthetic life, take control of the Reapers, or achieve Synthesis, leaks suggest that the game would have accounted for all of those possibilities somehow. According to Valente, ensuring that Universeâs handling of the endings âwouldn’t piss everyone offâ was one of BioWareâs big priorities. Despite years of fairweather fans saying BioWare should âjust make Destroy canon and move on,â that wasnât the route the studio wanted to take.

I don’t think it’s being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn’t piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn’t make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn’t privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel.

Not for nothing, guys, but that’s kind of a tall fucking order. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be really hard. An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn’t take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible…it takes a long time, and it’s not obvious how best to pull it off when you’re the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.

And it’s become really clear that it’s impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it’s easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a video game?

But we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place. There wasn’t one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can’t say any more than that.

I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I’d known when I finished ME3 that I’d be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess…

But as I’m saying a lot: yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there, because part of it was my job, and we tried our damnedest to do right by the story and the fandom. That room was full of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don’t think it could have been in better hands. We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it.

And I asked myself that at the end of everything I did: If I could go back to being just a fan, would I be happy with this?

Itâs nice to hear this sentiment again because I feel like the recent push for creators to just select one ending to make âcanonâ when creating sequels to choice-driven stories is more of a fan-driven impulse than it is a creator one. Often it feels rooted in a desire for more of a thing one likes at any cost, rather than in maintaining the integrity of the seriesâ role-playing and fiction, and usually in these situations, developers arenât looking for an easy way out. BioWare certainly wasnât, at least. Even during pre-release interviews for Dragon Age: The Veilguard, the studio was pretty adamant that it would rather not reference previous game choices than undermine them, though that would be impossible in a Mass Effect game set in the Milky Way after Mass Effect 3, given the galaxy-wide ramifications of the choices you make in that game.

Whatever Universeâs ambitions might have been for acknowledging all of Mass Effect 3âs endings, Valente also emphasized that the game wasnât done and that even the solutions the team was considering at this stage of development might not have been the ones used in the final game if it hadnât been canceled in favor of Star Wars Battlefront III.

âYou have to remember the game wasn’t done,â she wrote. âThings changed all the time, even week to week, and who knows where and how the things I worked on or saw others work on would have ended up in the final game. It’s forever frozen where it was when EA pulled its Renegade Interrupt, but that doesn’t mean that’s what it would have been without it.â

For now, Mass Effect fans are rallying around the #SaveMassEffect campaign that has amassed over 330,000 signatures in a Change.org petition, and has been putting billboards promoting the cause up in places like Times Square. Earlier this month, Canadian fans were able to successfully put forth a petition to be heard by the Canadian House of Commons, arguing that the Canadian government should help assist laid-off BioWare workers in buying the studio and its IP from EA, though any such deal would require the publisherâs cooperation.

#3618. Rockstar Games reveals 23 extra tracks in GTA 6's deluxe edition soundtrack, featuring Denzel Curry, HEALTH, and more

For those of you out there in love with Grand Theft Auto 6's soundtrack, you'll be happy to know that Rockstar Games have revealed an additional 23 tracks as part of the game's deluxe edition album.

These tracks, available via streaming services, include songs from artists like HEALTH, Denzel Curry, Playboi Carti, and more. You can find the full track list on the official Rockstar Games music website.

Some of these artists played a significant role in the game. Justice, for example, helped compose the game's original soundtrack and several of their tracks appear throughout the game. There are others, too.

Both Sexyy Red and Denzel Curry voice characters in the game's later chapters. Others like Kodack Black and Freddie Gibbs also show up, too - that's not to mention the huge number of musicians who make an appearance in the game's many radio stations. If you listen through those, you'll hear the voices of Keith Richards, Lana Del Ray, The Alchemist and others.

Musical talent also played an additional role in creating the TV advertisements and shows you can watch in the game. Zack Fox is one example, as is Weird Al Yankovic. Both wrote parts of the game's enticing and absurd big screen entertainment - which makes sense given the pair's shared comedy background.

If you're playing through the game right now, you may benefit from Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough, as well as the full list of GTA 6 cheats.

I cannot get over all the ways Rockstar has turned a controller into an immersion tool.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I hate to credit Sony's aggressive (and presumably very expensive) marketing campaign for GTA 6—you know, the one which appeared to have also plucked the ability for Xbox to even mention the game by name. That's something I'm still shocked was even a thing anyone was allowed to do.

So I won't credit it… mostly. We all already know that PC is going to get the best version of GTA 6 when it finally hits our desktops, whenever that might be. But I am going to agree with one part of the whole "Grand Theft Auto 6 plays best on PS5" shtick: the DualSense controller. It's so good that I fear those who reach for a mouse and keyboard will be missing out on some incredible immersion.

I never expected a controller to actively add to my experience, but I also forgot just how many goodies Sony stuffed into this thing. Seriously, Rockstar has taken full advantage of everything the peripheral has to offer.

I've been weaving through traffic way more in GTA 6 thanks to a huge increase in general vehicle density and some criminally narrow roads that can cause some major bottlenecks. Flooring it all the way from A to B isn't quite as easy as it used to be, which is why I kind of love how you can use the adaptive triggers to comfortably maintain a steady cruising speed before clicking it all the way in as a way to floor it. It makes my speed feel just that little more deliberate, with that tactile feel for when I really want to amp up how fast I'm going.

But driving might actually be the least interesting way Rockstar has made full use of the controller. The parts that have gotten me more than anything are the small ways haptics have been implemented to strengthen story moments or make parts of Leonida feel even more alive.

The first time I really noticed the controller was back in the beginning of the game, when I'm instructed to go and pick Lucia up from prison. As I'm standing outside as Jason, watching her emerge from the gate, the controller starts thumping just a little bit. A heartbeat. I'm literally feeling Jason's heart racing as Lucia approaches. No dialogue, no internal monologue letting me know how nervous he is. It's such a small detail, but one that massively hammed up the moment for me.

My absolute favourite way it's been implemented, though? The clubs. The goddamn clubs. Leonida's sprawling nightlife is already impressive in isolation—Hitman's Berlin level was the last time I felt this enamoured with a videogame nightclub—but this is where Rockstar went all-in on the controller's haptic feedback. Step into a club and you'll immediately feel the bass pulsating through the controller.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's not just the same, monorhythmic beat for every song though. The bass perfectly matches the song; those long, teeth-shaking booms cut with shorter, less intense thumps. I feel like I'm back in my first year of university trying to sleep while the nearby student nightclub blasts the same songs until 3am every damn Wednesday, the bass somehow reverberating across the campus and straight through my bedframe.

When I first set foot inside the Jack of Hearts club at the beginning of Chapter 3, I was practically stunlocked by how much more immersive being able to feel the bass through the controller was making the entire experience. Seriously, I cannot overstate just how much it sucks you into what's happening around you.

These are all things that I genuinely feel folks are going to miss out on with a simple mouse and keyboard. Sure, your aiming will be better. Yes, none of the things I've described above actually change anything about the gameplay. It'll still be the same GTA 6 no matter what you play with. But for all the ways Rockstar has managed to elevate the experience and the immersion I've been feeling just through something as small as the controller I'm holding? It at least deserves consideration for your go-to playthrough peripheral.

#3615. More than 39 million people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone, Sony says, as the game breaks all-time player numbers on the platform

Sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

In addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of new PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog says, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Microsoft hasn't announced equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

The merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery has resulted in the formation of Skydance, which now holds various high-profile media assets. From a news perspective, the David Ellison-led conglomerate now owns both CBS News and CNN. There’s been a considerable amount of discussion regarding the future of both entities, especially in regard to whether CBS’ Bari Weiss might run CNN. While Weiss won’t take that big seat, I’ve still been curious about a merger, and Ellison recently weighed in.

Given how internal mergers tend to happen following corporate consolidation, it is indeed reasonable to wonder whether CNN and CBS News might eventually be combined into a single entity. Ellison recently appeared at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit, where he discussed various facts of the company’s overall future. In terms of the corporation’s two marquee news banners, the exec was asked if there would be “a point a year from now, two years from now, where these institutions merge.” Ellison (via Deadline) said this:

Right now, we are incredibly happy operating them basically within the status quo. I think you also have … there might be some news sharing in the future. But right now we’re operating them as they are.

So this answer pretty much seems to fall into the category of “not a definitive yes, but not a definitive no”. At the very least, the possibility of “news sharing” does make sense due to the two networks now being under the same corporate umbrella. I still can’t help but wonder, however, whether Ellison isn't totally shutting down the merger idea due to it being internally discussed as a viable option. That’s just speculation on my part, of course, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the powers that be have or are currently pondering the idea, at the very least.

Ahead of the Paramount/WB merger, there were plenty of questions regarding what it might mean for CNN. Several media pundits expressed concerns about Weiss potentially being put in charge of the Ted Turner-founded political news network. W. Kamau Bell, a former host at the network, chastised Weiss’ handling of CBS News and argued that her presence would cause an issue with editorial autonomy. Those sentiments were echoed by another former analyst, Jim Acosta, who expressed his hope that Weiss wouldn’t “murder” CNN.

Bari Weiss Addresses 60 Minutes Concerns And How She’s Handling Backlash Against CBS News

Ellison eventually confirmed this past October, however, that current CNN CEO Mark Thompson would remain in his post. Shortly thereafter, Thompson spoke about the merger and shared some complimentary thoughts on his new bosses. The CEO said that after speaking to Ellison and the other Skydance executives, he felt “real confidence that they both understand and will fully support the principle and practice of the kind of independent news that CNN has always stood for.” All in all, Thompson has a solid reputation, and former CBS anchor Scott Pelley also praised him while warning CNN staffers about possible editorial changes post-merger.

As Thompson continues to run CNN, Bari Weiss will remain editor-in-chief at CBS News. Interestingly enough, Weiss was recently asked if she’d be interested in running CNN at some point, and she declared she was fine with solely overseeing her current network. It’s evident that the two media outlets will remain independent for now but, if David Ellison’s recent comments are anything to go by, Weiss and Thompson may have some editorial dealings down the road.

#3613. GTA 6 players are already starting to get very good at heists, despite all the new challenges Rockstar has added to the game

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

For one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

If you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

#3612. Christopher Lloyd, 88, Posts Tribute to Wife Lisa, 56, on 10th Anniversary

Christopher Lloyd is celebrating his 10th anniversary with his wife, Lisa Lloyd (née Loiacono).

In a Monday, November 23, X post, the Back to the Future star, 88, shared a photo of him and his wife decked in all black at a recent charity event in honor of his Back to the Future costar Michael J. Fox’s Parkinson’s research foundation.

He captioned the post, “Oh Lisa… I love you more than words can simply put. Happy anniversary to us now and always ❤️❤️❤️❤️.”

Lloyd met Lisa, 56, in 2005 and they tied the knot in 2016.

The actor was previously married four times, first to Catherine Boyd from 1959 until their divorce in 1971, Kay Tornborg from 1974 to 1987, Carol Ann Vanek from 1988 to 1991, and finally Jane Walker Wood, whom he wed in 1992 and divorced in 2005.

Earlier this month, the couple opened up about their marriage ahead of their 10th anniversary together.

“I appreciate his focus and his calmness. Because I’m very outgoing and gregarious. And sometimes he won’t talk. So it’s a balance,” Lisa praised the actor in a joint interview with People.

Lloyd added, “Well, Lisa says I’m kind of calm, even though I may be going crazy inside! But I think I’m pretty easy to live with, get along with.”

“He reads all day long,” Lisa also shared, noting that Lloyd doesn’t go online. “I’ve been with him almost 22 years. My head’s full with a bunch of stupid stuff that you see on the internet… I watch how contemplative and in control he can be, and I’ve always been more hyper and outgoing than him.”

Lloyd, meanwhile, praised Lisa as being “full of energy and excitement to do this and that. She’s far more naturally social than I am. I’m not a social bug by nature, and it just seems the gel just comes together.”

In his recent memoir, In My Own Time, Lloyd opened up about his past addiction to cocaine.

According to an excerpt published by Page Six, Lloyd took his first “snort” of the substance in the 1970s after meeting a woman at a comedy club in Los Angeles. The actor followed her to her car and they “did a couple of lines.”

“That was all it took. I was hooked almost immediately,” he wrote. “I loved it, and that was where my cocaine abuse began.”

“I wasn’t asking myself what it meant or what it was doing for me,” he added. “I just knew I liked it, and before long, it had a hold on me.”

#3611. Chatting With People In GTA Online About Why They’re Not Playing GTA 6: ‘$80 Is Too Much For Me, Bro’

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest video game on console right now. Everyone in my life, even people who don’t normally play these kinds of games, is booting up GTA 6 and spending hours exploring Vice City. But what about the people still playing GTA Online? What do they think of the newest entry which, for the time being, remains single-player? I dropped back into Rockstar’s existing multiplayer juggernaut a few days after GTA 6‘s launch to check out the vibes and ask people how they were feeling. The answers varied, but a surprisingly common response was that they were still playing GTA Online because they just couldn’t afford to buy GTA 6 right now.

GTA 5‘s live-service platform is still be very popular in 2026, but when I returned recently following the launch of GTA 6, it was definitely emptier than usual. I hopped into different sessions looking for players who were actually chatting on the mic, and found most lobbies to not be anywhere near close to full. In fact, many had only a few players hanging out in lobbies that support up to 30. I also ended up back in the same sessions again and again, which is not something that usually happens in GTA Online. And the sessions I landed in were filled with mostly low-level players and kids. A lot of the high-level kings and queens of GTA Online were missing. I assume they were chilling in Vice City.

One of the first people I spoke to was one of these GTA Online kids. They sounded no older than 12, and when I asked if they had played GTA 6, they told me no. I asked why and was told: “It sucks, bro.” I asked for more details, pretending I had yet to play it and was curious about it.

“It just sucks,” said the kid as he blew up a rival CEO. “I watched my cousin play it, bro, it just sucks. Likeâ¦it has good graphics, but GTA Online is more fun. It just sucks. That’s all I’m going to say about it, bro.â

Another player, who sounded a bit older, replied that “GTA 6 was shit” and that all the critics got “paid to glaze it.” Then he blew up the kid who said it sucked, and they started yelling at each other. At one point, the younger kid almost sounded like they were crying. It was awkward. Later, I ended up back in that session, and the kid who may have been crying was still very mad. Nobody else was talking in that session, so I hopped to a new one.

Eventually, I found a high-level player who was happy to chat. According to him, he desperately wants to play GTA 6, but money is tight.

“I gotta wait until I get paid again, dude,” the player told me over voice chat. “Iâve been waiting years…I can wait longer. I’m pretending I’m in GTA 6 right now. This chick next to me is Lucia. Or maybe Mandy!Â  Well, not as hot as her.” He laughed, and I asked if he’d been watching videos of GTA 6 while waiting to get paid and actually play it.Â

“Oh yeah, I’ve seen videos. Dude, it looks phenomenal. I can’t wait, man. But like, until then I’m here in GTA Online pretending it’s Vice City.” More laughter.

GTA Online is a community of players who will kill you in a heartbeat with a giant tank or flying car, but won’t ever say a single word to you before, during, or after. Shy little murderers. It’s been like this for years. So as I hopped from session to session, I also texted players via the in-game phone. It’s clunky, but I did get a few replies from people more willing to chat via text.

One person I texted, a level 7 player, confirmed that they just started playing GTA Online that very night. When I asked about GTA 6, they said they wanted to play, but it costs too much. So instead, the game’s historic launch inspired them to go back and finally give GTA Online a try. They had owned GTA 5 for a bit now and decided to kill time waiting for GTA 6 by making money in GTA Online. Another person I texted in-game simply told me GTA 6 looked boring and dumb. They apparently had no interest in playing it. Another player simply texted back, “$80 is too much for me, bro.”

In a different session, I found a gamer who claimed that everything they’d seen about GTA 6 made the game look “bad.”

“I don’t know, dude, seems boring,” said the player who sounded around my age. “Like I don’t wanna buy flowers for a girl and fix shit, bro. I wanna kill people and steal shit.” A moment later, that player yelled in anger as he was blown up by someone who was running around killing anyone they spotted with a flying motorcycle.Â

As I wrapped up my time back in GTA Online, I heard more kids yelling at each other about stealing drugs or something. In the background, I heard one kid yell out that he was going to invite someone else. The kid he was going to invite began screaming and crying in the background. “I don’t want to play GTA 5 ONLINE!”

Another person joked that he must want to play GTA 6 instead. And then he added: “My parents won’t buy GTA 6 for me because it’s, like, filled with boobs and shit.”

After playing GTA Online again and chatting with more people over voice and text, what I learned is that while some players are staying away from GTA 6 because of silly complaints about it being woke, the vast majority of players either don’t care about that or have no idea some online are complaining about that crap. Instead, the real reason most of them aren’t playing GTA 6 is simply that they don’t have the money to buy it right now. And many of them really want to play it.Â  That sucks for them, but it’s good news for Take-Two and Rockstar. GTA 6 is already selling incredibly well, and if my time in GTA Online has revealed one thing, it’s that even more people are going to be buying it soon once they can afford it.

Take Out Kitty Litter for Tyrone across the Vice City.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Taking Out Kitty Litter's lab locations in GTA 6 is a mission in Tyrone's questline, and sees you searching the city for 18 secret labs (after the first one he directs you to). Every lab has a red smoking chimney and a blue and white Spin On This laundry van parked outside.

It'll take a little while, but it's well worth it to get the unique gold SMG at the end. Plus, Tyrone will start buying narcotics from you for the highest price possible. To destroy each lab, simply shoot a smoking pink flask and then run away. I've also laid these out in the most optimal order, separated into regions, so you're not driving back and forth across Vice City.

Last note: if you want to unlock map markers for the labs yourself versus relying on these videos, you can threaten cooks in certain labs to potentially reveal them.

After you complete some missions for Tyrone (when you meet him with Dre'Quan during Dealer's Choice) he'll direct you to this trailer park in La Perle where you destroy the first Kitty Litter lab and start the hunt for the others. You can see the route to the lab in the video above.

You can find this one in the trailer park opposite Zenon's Pawn Shop Ammu-Nation in La Perle. As soon as you go through the main gate, you can see the trailer with the funnel chimney where they're cooking straight ahead. Sneak around the back and break inside to find the lab. Or take out the three guys in front and go in that way.

Just across the road from the Mezzasega Espresso and Slinger in the Decor District. Pull off to the right of the road into the Williams + Whitaker Homeware and Decor car park. You'll see a garage with a shutter at the far end with a smoking chimney and the laundry van parked. Open the shutter to find a lone guy in the lab.

This one is behind Peterson's Autoshop in Rockridge, directly south across the road from the Blessed Food Market, under the overpass, on the border between Rockridge and La Perle. Head through the main yard and turn left to spot the laundry van. Break into it, move it forward, and open the shutter behind to find the lab.

Just east of Fleeca Field stadium, next door to Xero Gas - Rockridge. You'll spot the blue and white laundry van parked off to the side of the road behind a wall. Head down that alley and turn right to find a garage door you can open with the lab inside.

On the east side of the condominium building directly south of the Vice City Hospital, by Emilio's Auto Center Gas. Look for the closed road with the laundry van parked at the southern end and some staircases and flats off to the side with the chimney spewing smoke. The lab is through the white door on the bottom floor.

Just down the road to the west of Bump and Grind coffee and Salon Belle, in a block of flats southeast of Fleeca Fields stadium. You can see the laundry van parked outside. The lab is on the upper floor on the left side in apartment 5, where you can see the smoking chimney. Break in via the front door to find the lab.

This lab is an easy one to find, around the back of Cross My Heart Tattoos. Head around the right side, turn left, and look to your left for the garage door with the guy sitting down guarding it, with the lab inside.

This lab is in the block of flats to the southeast of the Jack of Hearts and Urban Legendz, with the laundry van parked out front. Look inside apartment 103 on the first floor on the left side. It's quite hard to get away from this lab blowing up, so shoot it from outside and run away. Also this will likely cause a big shootout in the block, so book it.

This lab is to the southwest of your apartment in Chapter 3 and to the east of the Crosstown Mule - City Line marker. Look for an overgrown lot with the laundry van parked in it. The garage with the lab is just behind that.

This lab is directly west of Down Town Pawn, just between Rideout Customs and the Vargo's Gas station. Just past the gas station, look to the left where its fuel sign is to spot a laundry van, and further down the track, the garage with the lab and smoking chimney above it.

This lab is close to Xero Gas - Tequesta and west of Vice Seven Condominiums gym. When driving east to west past the station, turn right and keep an eye on your right towards the two floored condominiums for the laundry van parked outside. You want the set of staircases to the right of the van. Take the right side one up to the first floor to find the lab door directly ahead.

This lab is in a trailer park directly east down the road from Arrow Gas - VCIA, also west under the bridge from Pawn City and Vice City Firearms. Turn into the trailer park, take the first right and drive a little way around the corner to spot the trailer with the smoking chimney on the left. You can enter via a window around the other side to find the lab.

This lab is located in the far south of Salton, north of the Pay 'N' Spray - Salton, next door to the Slator Towing Inc robbery. Go around the south side of the derelict block of flats and climb the dumpster to jump up through the open window to find the lab.

This lab is west down the road from Xero Gas - Salton. Cross the train tracks, then keep an eye on your right for a carpark with a blue and white laundry van, then turn right into it to spot the building with the smoking chimney on the right. Hop the fence straight ahead and turn right to find one guy guarding the garage with the lab.

This lab is easy to find, directly south of Salon Perez and Safia Restaurant in Little Cuba. Look for some bungalows on the left with the laundry van parked outside. It's in the building with the chimney to the left of the one the van is parked in front of. The lab is the second door along.

This lab is north up the road from the Pay 'N' Spray - Balsero. Turn left down the alley with the laundry van parked to find a guy guarding the gate, a couple of guys inside, and the lab in an open garage further back behind them.

This lab is in a trailer park southeast from the Balasero jewelry stores, across the river. If driving from the east and the city, turn left before the bridge, turn right, then turn left and head a little way down to spot the trailer with the funnel chimney and laundry van outside. Sneak around back to get in and find the lab.

This lab is south across the river from Ron's Car Wash and Gas. Head over the bridge, across the junction, then keep an eye out to your left to spot where the laundry van is parked. The lab is just in the building beyond the gate with the smoking chimney. The door requires a code which is 1999 (referencing the billboard up to the right).

There are three main advantages to destroying all the Kitty Litter labs and completing the Spin On This mission with Tyrone and those are:

You'll also get $2,000 a lab, plus $10,000 for the Spin On This mission, meaning $48,000 altogether. Since I did everything, it's unclear to me whether these rewards are for destroying every lab, or the mission specifically that you get after you destroy 15 of them. Either way, if you want all of this, destroy all the labs in the city and complete the mission.

#3609. Rockstar is actively shopping Red Dead Redemption movie and TV rights around, just don't expect the same for Grand Theft Auto

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a new report, the company is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

The information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the company is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of shows based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

Indeed, many more video game-based shows are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

But none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

Warning! The following contains spoilers from the 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way episode "The Parent Trapped." Stream the episode with an HBO Max subscription, and read at your own risk!

Jonathan Pearce and Ally Yahuff's scene with her parents kicking her out after revealing her pregnancy was heartbreaking, but as her parents have allegedly stated on social media, it was scripted. As 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way cut to Ally crying in bed, her parents hopped on social media to give the alleged truth behind this storyline.

For those who missed the latest episode on the 2026 TV schedule, Jonathan and Ally met with her parents and sister and broke the news about the pregnancy. The episode then cut to a scene of the city, with text explaining that her parents refused to participate in filming after they revealed the news. Now we're learning that's allegedly not entirely true, as they have become the latest subjects to accuse the TLC series of faking scenes.

Ally's parents replied to a comment on a social media post made by 90 Day Fiancé fan @NathanTemp2 and laid out what they allege happened after Jonathan dropped the news. As it turns out, their story is completely different than what was shown in the episode. Check it out below (via @KikiandKibbitz):

This is not true at all. We took the pregnancy very well. We are very happy. We have been spending quality time with Ally, Jon, and the baby for almost 7 months now. What disappointed us was the fact that the whole storyline is revolving around us, the parents, not knowing about the pregnancy, when we already knew! We just played along.

The comment went on to state that they were under the impression the storyline was solely about Jonathan and Ally, but agreed to filming despite being uncomfortable on camera. They did ask TLC to omit the footage, but it had nothing to do with Ally's pregnancy and more their discomfort replaying that moment for television.

Now, it's always important to note that this information is still alleged, and Ally's parents could be stating this to save face after what was originally shown in 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way. Conversely, I did wonder why Jonathan and Ally would need to tell them the news when she was clearly showing.

The new information presents conflicting accounts of what happened with Jonathan and Ally, and makes me question why she was so upset afterward. If that scene was also scripted, then I'm also wondering if all the red flags that we saw were also just for the show.

90 Day Fiancé’s David Dangerfield Spoke Out After Former Fiancé Sheila Mangubat Died

This is what always happens when these conflicting stories crop up. Now I'm questioning everything that we've seen in Jonathan and Ally's storyline, and wondering what's real and what wasn't. Are the parents even telling the truth? Is anyone telling the truth?

What it sounds like is the producers wanted to recreate the scene in which Ally initially told her parents she was pregnant for the sake of the storyline. Past vets have said that's a common thing, and that it can often lead to arguments when family has to rehash past trauma.

All this to say, I'm going to be keeping a much closer eye on what's happening with Jonathan and Ally going forward. I'd also love to see if these online comments will be addressed in the tell-all special, or 90 Day Fiancé's producers will hope the drama fades before then.

Catch 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way on TLC on Sundays at 8:00 p.m. ET. This season has been very entertaining thus far, especially now that we have a great update on Armando Rubio's daughter after that scary scene.

#3606. Unofficial GTA 6 PC port effort suffers setback as Rockstar seemingly takes down Project Leonida, one of the internet's biggest recompilation projects

A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."

Before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

Incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

Rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not announced GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

It's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers, getting hunted down by killer NPCs, and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?

My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.

So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.

The fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.

But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.

I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.

Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.

I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Rockstar amped up the mayhem and carnage you could cause, turning it into a chaotic playground with few repercussions. GTA Online players have become accustomed to walking around like some vengeful god, wreaking havoc wherever or whenever they see fit, and only very occasionally dealing out mercy. Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.

A part of me understands the appeal. Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while. NPCs that actually have a backbone offer an experience that will keep me interested for far longer.

Plus, Leonida is based on Florida, do you honestly think you could terrorise the streets of Miami or Tampa Bay and walk out completely unscathed? Yeah, I thought as much.

Hallmark churns out nearly a hundred new romance movies every year. The 2026 Countdown to Christmas lineup alone is slated for 34 original holiday-themed flicks. Part of the reason it’s easy for the cable channel-turned-streamer to make so many movies a year is that it has a list of dedicated actors who are eager to star in these films -- like Queen of Hallmark Lacey Chabert. And yet, somehow, they manage to keep the pairings fresh. So fresh that two of my favorite longtime Hallmark actors, Erin Cahill and Andrew Walker, just starred in their first movie together. I’m happy to report it was worth the wait!

Yep, you read that right. After spending 20 years with the cable channel and being friends for 18 years, Cahill and Walker finally got to share the screen as romantic leads in Christmas in Blue Dog Valley. The holiday flick follows Goldie MacKenzie (Cahil), a former Hollywood on-set veterinarian, who decides to leave the glitz and glamour for a slower life as the in-house veterinarian in the small town of Blue Dog Valley.

The residents of Blue Dog Valley aren’t too thrilled about an outsider taking over their beloved veterinary practice, and Goldie has to work overtime to win over the hearts of the town’s loyal pet owners. Desperate for an ally, Goldie turns to Cohen (Walker), the son of the former owner of the vet practice, for help. While they get off to a rough start, sparks start to fly as the two spend more time together, especially with Goldie taking over planning duties for the annual Christmas parade that will feature the four-legged and furry residents of the town this year.

It’s not just their characters who have love for each other, though. Both Cahill and Walker have a deep appreciation for each other and their decades-long friendship. In talking with Hallmark on set, both of these iconic stars shared how excited they were to be sharing the screen together for the first time. Take a look:

A post shared by Hallmark Channel (@hallmarkchannel)

It can be easy for the human actors to get upstaged by their animal co-stars, especially when there are so many different types of animals in a movie (cows, alpacas, and of course dogs in this case), but Cahill and Walker managed to hold things down even in the face of an adorable, overweight corgi. It’s a testament to the chemistry these two have on screen.

Their characters don’t share as much time on screen together as some of the other couples in Hallmark’s Christmas movies. However, the time they are together is swoonworthy — well, once they got over their meet-cute, that is. I definitely wouldn’t mind a sequel revisiting Goldie and Cohen a year from now. Or, better yet, I’d love to see Cahill and Walker star in even more Hallmark movies together now that it’s clear that they play compelling and entertaining romantic leads.

Blue Dog Valley might not be my favorite Hallmark Christmas movie of 2026, but it's still worth the watch. If you missed the live airing, you can stream it now with an active Hallmark+ subscription. While there, check out my favorite Cahill movie, Christmas on Cherry Lane, or my favorite Walker film, Three Wise Men and a Baby.

#3603. Today's Nintendo Switch Online update finally introduces a feature players have been asking for since 2018

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

This new option arrived fairly quietly as part of an update that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a big deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the new update, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

"Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," says one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

In order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?"

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" says another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

#3602. The Plan Was For Mass Effect: Universe To Tell You What Happened To All Your Favorite Characters

Mass Effect: Universe was still in early concept phases when it was canceled last month, but it sounds like the team at BioWare was paying a lot of attention to how the game would connect to the original trilogy, despite the apparent 600-year time jump. Handling Mass Effect 3âs divergent endings was one thing, but what about the beloved crewmates players wouldnât have seen since Mass Effect 3? Well, it sounds like BioWare was planning on giving players at least a hint of what they missed in the centuries between Shepardâs story and the fifth game.

Catherynne M. Valente, the writer of the novel Mass Effect Andromeda: Annihilation and one of the writers who was working on Universe before BioWare was shut down, is still under NDA and canât talk about too many specifics, but she is being as candid as she can be about the time she spent working with BioWare on fifth game in a Mass Effect Reddit AMA. There, sheâs been answering some questions fans have about how the game would have handled continuity, and one interesting thing she brings up is that the writing team had been talking about what happened to various characters in the time between the trilogy and Universe.Â

Liara TâSoni, a squadmate in the first and third games (and a temporary one in Mass Effect 2âs Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC) had already been confirmed to appear in the game, which made sense because she is an Asari, which are notoriously long-lived compared to most other Mass Effect aliens, and because she canât die in the existing ME games unless you get a âbadâ ending in Mass Effect 3. But what about Grunt, a member of the similarly long-lived Krogan species, or EDI, an advanced AI that likely remains alive as long as Shepard didnât destroy all Synthetic life at the end of ME3? Well, it sounds like BioWare was considering those questions, but Valente stops short of confirming they would have appeared.

âI think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically could survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them,â she wrote. âWe thought about all the things you’d have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it’s the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously.â

Elsewhere, Valente was asked if players would have been able to learn what happened to squadmates after the Reaper War in Mass Effect 3, and she says that part of her work on Universe was to write those fates and variations, and that players would have been able to learn what happened in the 600 years between.

Asked if she had âheadcanonsâ about the fates of those characters, she replied, âNo, darling, I don’t have headcanons about those fates, I have canon-canons. I know you’d have been able to find out about them because one of my jobs was to write all those fates and their possible variations all then submitted to the room, workshopped with everyone, and sent to higher-ups for approval. When I went on hiatus I was still waiting for approval on some of them, so I can’t even say for sure that I would have gotten a yes on a few. But I did on many of them. In fact, the whole reason I got that assignment was that, in a different Thing I was working on, I included the potential fate(s) of an original squadmate and did an impressive enough job with it to be trusted with the rest.)

God, it was like being asked to stitch a nice border on the Shroud of Turin. I put on my Big Writer Pants for that one and gave it every bit of talent I have, because I love those characters beyond measure, and they more than earned my best.

You think I could find it in my soul to disappoint my Commander? Never.â

Valenteâs AMA may not be able to get into too many specifics, but it sheds some light on what BioWareâs plans were before Mass Effect: Universe was canceled. She even mentions that new alien races were in the works, which would have been exciting to see considering Mass Effect: Andromeda only included one new alien race in the Angara.Â

Although Mass Effect: Universe isnât coming out, the folks who helped make BioWareâs most memorable games are still making cool stuff elsewhere for you to check out.
